meta.title: Support
meta.description: Get help with Bookmark Scout: answers to common problems, how to report a bug, and where to email about support, privacy, and security.

supportPage.title: Support
supportPage.intro: Most answers are in the docs and the FAQ. If something is broken, report it on GitHub. For anything you would rather not post in public, email us.

docs.title: Read the docs
docs.body: Installation for each browser, feature guides, and every setting explained.

faq.title: Check the FAQ
faq.body: Short answers about where your data goes, whether you need AI, and what works in Firefox.

firefoxRestart.q: Bookmark Scout disappears when I restart Firefox
a: Until the Firefox Add-ons listing is live, Bookmark Scout runs in Firefox as a temporary add-on, and Firefox removes temporary add-ons when it restarts.
Load it again after a restart: open about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox, click Load Temporary Add-on, and select the manifest.json file in the extracted folder.

firefoxManager.q: I can't find the bookmarks manager in Firefox
a: Firefox does not let extensions replace its bookmarks page, so the Bookmark Scout manager and its Tools sidebar are not available there. The maintenance tools, import and export, saved searches, statistics, and the AI tools in the manager work in Chrome and Edge.
In Firefox, use the toolbar popup to search, save pages, and manage folders.

firefoxIcons.q: Site icons are missing in Firefox
a: Bookmark Scout shows the browser's own cached icons, which Chrome and Edge share with extensions and Firefox does not. Sites you have not visited recently can show a generic globe in Chrome and Edge for the same reason.

Run Refresh Site Icons in the manager's Tools sidebar to download each site's own icon. Saved icons stay on this device. In Firefox the manager opens only at its extension URL; the documentation explains how to find it.

websiteAccess.q: Check Dead Links, Metadata Fetcher, or Refresh Site Icons did not scan anything
a: These tools need access to websites, which Bookmark Scout does not get at install. The browser asks the first time you run them, and if you decline, nothing is scanned.
Run the tool again and allow access when the browser asks.

aiSetup.q: AI features are missing or do not respond
a: AI features are off by default. Turn them on in Settings, under AI, choose a provider, and enter your API key. A local Ollama server needs no key.
Click Verify Service to test the connection. The first time, the browser asks for access to that provider's site; allow it so the extension can reach the provider.

report-a-bug.title: Report a bug
report-a-bug.body: Bug reports go to GitHub Issues, where anyone can follow the fix. Search the existing issues first, in case someone has already reported it.

include.browser: Your browser and its version (Chrome, Edge, or Firefox).
include.version: The Bookmark Scout version, shown on your browser's extensions page.
include.steps: The steps that lead to the problem, starting from where you opened Bookmark Scout: the popup, side panel, or manager.
include.result: What you expected and what happened instead, including any error message.
include.screenshot: A screenshot if it helps, with private bookmarks hidden.

report-a-bug.privacyNote: Issues are public. Never paste an API key, and leave out bookmark titles or URLs you do not want others to see.

support.title: Help with the extension
support.body: Questions about installing or using Bookmark Scout that you would rather not post in public.

privacy.title: Privacy questions and requests
privacy.body: Questions about how your data is handled. The <privacyPolicy>privacy policy</privacyPolicy> explains what the extension and the websites do with data.

security.title: Security vulnerabilities
security.body: Report vulnerabilities here privately, not in a public issue. See <securityPolicy>SECURITY.md</securityPolicy> and <securityTxt>security.txt</securityTxt>.
